simple.meaning: נָבַב (nâbab) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to pierce ; to be hollow , or (figuratively) foolish.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 4 times in Exodus, Job, Jeremiah, beginning at Exodus 27:8. The surrounding contexts include altar, mountain.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נָבַב (H5014) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: נָבַב (nâbab) / H5014 is traced through Exodus 27:8, Exodus 38:7, Job 11:12, Jeremiah 52:21 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to pierce ; to be hollow , or (figuratively) foolish
definitions.full: H5014. nabab [ נָבַב ] verb hollow out (compare Assyrian imbubu , flute , Dl HWB 443 , Late Hebrew אַבּוּב id. , Aramaic אַבּוּבָא id. ; hence also Arabic knots in reed, part of reed between knots, reed ; see Hoffm LCB 1882, 321 Frä 23 Fl in Levy TW i. 417 ); — Qal Passive participle נָבוּב Job 11:12 ; Jer 52:21 ; נְבוּב Exod 27:8 ; 38:7 ; — hollowed, hollow: of altar of tabernacle לֻחוֺת נְבוּב 27:8 ; 38:7 (P); of pillar in temple Jer 52:21 ; figurative נָבוּב אִישׁ Job 11:12 , i.e. empty, hollow-minded man. נֹ֫בֶה see נֹב .

occurrences.englishText: You shall make it hollow with planks. They shall make it as it has been shown you on the mountain.
He put the poles into the rings on the sides of the altar, with which to carry it. He made it hollow with planks.

As for the pillars, the height of the one pillar was eighteen cubits;* A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters. and a line of twelve cubits encircled it; and its thickness was four fingers. It was hollow.
